questions.question: The approximate harmonic mean of 8, 6, 12, 4 is:
questions.questionHtml: The approximate harmonic mean of 8, 6, 12, 4 is:
questions.solution:
Key Points Harmonic Mean: 

  • The central tendency of a group of numbers is determined using the Harmonic Mean, a type of average.
  • Smaller values in the set are given more weight by the harmonic mean.
  • Since it considers the inverse relationship between two variables, the harmonic mean is very helpful when working with rates or ratios.
  • Harmonic Mean = n / [1/x1 + 1/x2 + 1/x3 + ... + 1/xn]

Important Points 

Given:

n = 4

a = 8, b = 6, c = 12 and d = 4

n = number of observation

a, b, c, d are observations

Formula:

Harmonic mean

= \(\frac{n}{\frac{1}{a}+\frac{1}{b}+\dots +\frac{1}{n^{th}\ term}}\)

Calculation:

Harmonic mean

= \(\frac{4}{\frac{1}{8}+\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{12}+\frac{1}{4}}\)

= \(\frac{4}{\frac{3+4+2+6}{24}}\)

= (24 × 4)/15 = 32/5

= 6.4

∴ The harmonic mean of these observations is 6.40

 

The harmonic mean is the reciprocal of arithmetic mean

questions.question: If an event B has occurred and has P(B) = 1, the conditional probability P(A|B) is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: If an event B has occurred and has P(B) = 1, the conditional probability P(A|B) is equal to:
questions.solution:
Explanation

If the event B occurs does not change the probability that event A occurs, and event A and B are the independent event then

⇒ P(A I B) = P(A)

According to bayes’s theorem It states the relation between the probabilities of A and B, P(A) and P(B) and the conditional probabilities of A gives B and B gives A.

⇒ P(A I B) and P(B I A)

⇒ P(A I B) = P(B I A).P(A)/P(B)

⇒ P(B I A) = P(A ∩ B)/P(A)

⇒ P(A ∩ B) = P(A).P(B)

⇒ P(A I B) = P(A ∩ B).P(A)/P(A). P(B)

⇒ P(A I B) = P(A). P(B).P(A)/P(A).P(B)

⇒ P(A I B) = P(A)

∴ The value of P(A I B) is P(A)

It is necessary to determine the number of possible outcomes

Subjective approach = “In the subjective approach we define probability as the degree of belief that we hold in the occurrence of an event”

The sources from where we get information are called data sources and these may comprise documents, humans, institutions as well as mass media like newspapers, radio, television, etc.

  • All recorded sources of information irrespective of their contents and forms come under documentary sources which can be categorized based on their content into primary, secondary, and tertiary sources of data.

Key Points

  • Secondary data refers to data that is collected by someone other than the primary user.
  • It means that the information is already available, and someone analyses it.
  • The secondary sources include magazines, newspapers, books, journals, censuses information collected by the government dept, organizational records, and data that was originally collected for other research purposes.
  • For example, Suppose we want to know the number of persons in different income groups in a particular village. For this, the figures will be available with the Municipality / Panchayat Office. This is an example of data collected from secondary sources.

Hence, the data taken from the published report on dropouts from school will be considered as secondary data.

Hint

  • Primary Sources refer to the sources which contain original/first-hand material or fresh information.

An ogive is a curve that shows the cumulative frequency distribution of a dataset, with X-coordinates representing the upper limits of the class interval and Y-coordinates representing the corresponding cumulative frequency. A histogram is a graphical display of data using bars of different heights, with each bar grouping numbers into ranges. A straight line graph is formed when an equation can be rearranged into the form y = mx + c. Two independent events A and B

We need to find P(A - B).

P(A - B) = P(A)(1 - P(B))
